new_material: Food matters as well as weapons: the caveman’s energy drains with hunger. Enemies leave food to replenish it. Some stages offer a choice of routes, although those paths lead to the same boss.

Emulator programmer Miguel Ángel Horna recalled how the project began. He was collaborating with Miguel Ángel Pastor on the Dreamcast emulator Chankast when Zeebo approached Pastor. Zeebo had licensed Data East games, including Caveman Ninja, but the pair still had to implement the emulator needed to run them.

The Mexican edition is recorded on 31 March 2010. In Brazil, Lucas Mousinho reported on 17 April that the game had appeared on ZeeboNet the previous day, one day ahead of its announced schedule. It cost 1,290 Z-Credits.
Mousinho welcomed its weapons, branching routes and two-player adventure, placing it among his favourite Zeebo games at that point.

new_material: Arcade play unlocks hidden fighters, Survival tests how many opponents one life bar can overcome, and Training provides room to practise combinations. Versus supports a second player. The Zeebo edition has Portuguese menu text, but no individual character ending movies.
Before launch, John Rizzo said it was not a mobile conversion, but could not identify which earlier platform supplied the port.

Mig64 expected little from the slow-looking trailer. After playing the released game, he described much smoother animation, responsive controls and a useful choice of D-pad or analog movement. Missing character voices and endings disappointed him. He initially undervalued its replay appeal, then revised that part after repeatedly returning to play.

Writing as an owner in 2019, Douglas Deiró also regretted the absent endings, but valued the full fighter roster and the revised character models. He considered the remaining game worth playing on the console he actually owned.

new_material: Alongside local two-player chess, there are ordinary and timed games against the computer. Winning earns gears, the in-game currency spent on pieces, boards, backgrounds, tutorials and analyses of historical matches. Players can also stake their gears on a game for a larger reward.

In January 2009, Zeebo CEO John Rizzo said the conversion from Glu’s BREW version had taken four months. He described a proposed wireless two-player edition as manageable because only the moves needed transmitting.

new_material: The controller supports both single-button moves and some combined-button commands. Weapons can be dropped deliberately, while dashing and launch attacks can be linked into mid-air combinations. Rockman’s detailed Zeebo review made those juggling attacks a particular attraction.

Access itself became part of the game’s history. Double Dragon Dojo contributor Rockman described buying a Brazilian Zeebo through an auction site, using Google Translate, and finding one with Double Dragon already installed. He praised its fighting options, enemy roster and unlockable Extra mode.

A review reproduced at Zeebo Club in March 2010 was more reserved about the fighting. It praised the redrawn sprites but described attack sequences that could not be cancelled, leaving a fighter exposed when punches missed. The writer considered the result enjoyable, with less fluid combat than it could have had.
